message.content:
Below is an overview of **long‑weekend** periods in Canada for the calendar year 2023 – i.e., statutory holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday (or create a “bridge” day) so that you end up with at least three consecutive non‑working days.  
(If your province has additional provincial holidays not listed here, those will also generate extra long weekends.)

| Date | Holiday | Day of Week | Long Weekend |
|------|---------|-------------|--------------|
| Jan 1 – Jan 2 | New Year’s Day / Family Day (AB & BC) | Sun/Monday | *New Year’s* (Sun‑Mon) |
| Feb 20 | Louis Riel Day (MB) | Fri | *Louis Riel* (Fri‑Sat) |
| Mar 17 | St. Patrick’s Day (NL) | Sat | — |
| Apr 7 | Good Friday | Fri | *Good Friday* (Fri‑Sat) |
| Apr 10 | Easter Sunday | Mon | — |
| May 22 | Victoria Day | Mon | *Victoria* (Thu‑Sat) |
| Jun 19 | National Indigenous Peoples Day | Tue | — |
| Jul 1 | Canada Day | Thu | — |
| Aug 15 | Civic Holiday (BC), Labour Day (other provinces) | Mon | *Labour/Civic* (Fri‑Mon) |
| Sep 4 | Thanksgiving (Canada) | Mon | *Thanksgiving* (Fri‑Mon) |
| Oct 9 | Heritage Day (ON) | Fri | *Heritage* (Fri‑Sat) |
| Nov 11 | Remembrance Day | Wed | — |
| Dec 25 | Christmas Day | Mon | *Christmas* (Fri‑Mon) |
| Dec 26 | Boxing Day | Tues | — |

### How it works

A “long weekend” usually means:

1. A statutory holiday falls on a **Friday**, giving you a four‑day break from Thursday evening through Saturday night.  
2. A statutory holiday falls on a **Monday**, giving you a four‑day break from Friday afternoon through Tuesday morning.  
3. If a holiday falls on a **Tuesday/Wednesday/Thursday**, many people take a bridge day (e.g., Wednesday off) to extend the weekend—though this isn’t mandatory.

For example:
- **May 22 (Victoria Day)** gives you a classic long weekend because it lands on a Monday.  
- **Aug 15 (Civic/Labour Day)** creates another one as it’s always observed on the first Monday in August across most provinces.

---

#### Quick Reference List (by month)

| Month | Long‑Weekend Dates (Holiday) |
|-------|-------------------------------|
| January | Jan 1 (Sunday) → Jan 2 (Monday) |
| February | Feb 20 (Friday) |
| April | Apr 7 (Friday) |
| May | May 22 (Monday) |
| June | None |
| July | None |
| August | Aug 15 (Monday) |
| September | Sept 4 (Monday) |
| October | Oct 9 (Friday) |
| November | None |
| December | Dec 25 (Monday) |

> **Tip:** For a fully automated integration, consider using a reliable API service that provides official Canadian holiday calendars per province (many services offer JSON endpoints).

Let me know if you'd like the same breakdown broken down by individual provinces or territories!
